However, this medicine has been used for a double digit number of years in something like over 40 countries and there haven't been any cases of that, that I could find.

[W6D5] I feel like most of the big things I had been experiencing have either died down very significantly or have diminished away completely this week. Colors seem to be back to their normal volume, the dreams seem to be back to regular dreams, and back to waking up normally (I used to wake up exhausted the first few weeks). Let me note, these things have been gradually diminishing over the past couple of weeks, relative to the first couple of weeks, but it seems that everything is "back to normal" by the end of this week. Still no real noticeable benefits to report.

[side note] I had talked to my father about this and he was curious enough to give it a go himself; this is the end of his first week of 2mL @ 5/wk dosing, ie., [W1D5]. Save that he thought his vision was a little sharper on the third day (but not the fourth) he hasn't noticed anything yet.

[W7D6] Meh. Still can't speak to any noticeable benefits re memory or focus. The crazy dreams came back this week a couple of times. I will say that there does seem to be a slightly noticeable effect in regards to anxiety, it seems like it takes the edge off a bit. I've been hesitant to say it earlier because I wasn't sure I wasn't just imagining it; but as I said earlier, my father just finished his 2nd week and he told me it seemed like it was easier for him to do public speaking, that he had a better grasp on what he wanted to say without the anxiety of the event interfering with his thought processes. Other than that (and some weird dreams), he hadn't noticed anything else, not even the colors being brighter (lower dose though, 2mL vs my 5mL). He only opted for a 2wk course, so he's done, but I'll post any other updates he gives me.

[W8D3] Done. I finished 2 days early, but that's because I dropped a box of Cer. and broke two vials.

Semi-Final Verdict: meh, didn't do shit for memory or focus, but it did give me some of the most complex, detailed, realistic, strongly emotional, and longest dreams of my life. No joke, I feel like the movie Inception was on to something, there were dreams that I had which seemed to last several days, I would wake up exhausted with a headache but full of all these new ideas and things to think about. It obviously does stuff, and even if it didn't do what it "should have" done I don't regret doing it.

Is it worth the almost $400 (including syringes, needles, etc.)? Well, it's your brain...you probably spent that much money on a cellphone just to keep it entertained throughout the day, what's the big downside to spending that much on something that actually does more than entertain it? It's like eating vegetables; you don't feel any different after eating them, but they're still good for you.

The biggest potential downside would be the actual injections. I honestly don't care about poking myself with needles like some people, but 38+ self-injections (sometimes you just hit a nerve or something and have to start over in a different spot) over 8 weeks (even spread out over 6 individual muscles like I did) is still enough to leave you with occasional scabs and bruises, then there's also the worry of potential infection.

I'll post an actual Final Verdict in 1-2 weeks, after I've had some time to see what happens to me after the injections stopped.

[W10D6] 17 days after final injection. So, my final verdict: worth it.

  • I'm still relatively young, in my prime some would say, so i wasn't expecting much out of it, and I didn't think much was going on during the injections, but the 2+weeks since the injections I have felt a noticeably longer time for memory recall compared to how it was 2-4 weeks ago.

  • I still get the occasional amazing dreams too, but nowhere near as often.

  • My attention might have improved a little, probably equivalent to the tune of taking 2.5-5mg of adderall...which in itself is a subjective comparison, but it's the best form of comparison I can give.

  • As far as memory retention...nothing there to report. I'll forget someones name 5 seconds after they tell it to me. Not that my memory is shot to shit, I've always had trouble remembering peoples names and faces, it's just exactly the same as it was prior to the injections.

  • I've started sleeping less now too; on the Cer. I could black out sleep for 8hrs easy, even had a few 10hr nights and one 12hr night (and woke up groggy every damn day), but I'm back to 5-6hrs a night now with the occasional 8hr night. The grogginess is gone now too.

  • (edit, new bullet: forgot to mention this, the irony) Anxiety levels have noticeably dropped. In fact you could say I no longer have anxiety...ever. Not that I had bad anxiety prior to this; but you know, the occasional anxiety when being put into new situations or starting up conversations with new people. Yeah, that's all gone now. I started working at a new place a couple of weeks ago, within 2-3 days I had already befriended everybody on staff there and am now on a first name basis with people above me in the food chain (people who's names start with "Dr."). I guess I should start thinking of ways to exploit this now. Ideas would be appreciated.
